title: Vector Databases
subtitle: Embeddings, similarity search, and vector stores

content.text: Vector databases store embeddings and perform approximate nearest-neighbour search to find semantically similar content.

content.code:
from chromadb import Client
import chromadb

client = chromadb.Client()
collection = client.create_collection("docs")

# Add documents (ChromaDB embeds automatically)
collection.add(
    documents=["Redis is an in-memory data store", "MongoDB is a document database"],
    ids=["doc1", "doc2"]
)

# Query
results = collection.query(
    query_texts=["What is Redis?"],
    n_results=1
)
print(results["documents"])

content.definition: A vector (list of floats) representing the semantic meaning of text. Similar texts have similar vectors.

content.text: For production, use managed vector DBs like Pinecone, Weaviate, or pgvector (Postgres extension).

questions.question: What does a vector database use to find similar documents?
questions.explanation: Vector databases compute cosine similarity (or dot product) between query and document embeddings to find semantic matches.

faq.q: What embedding model should I use?
faq.a: For English-only use cases, text-embedding-3-small (OpenAI) is fast and cheap. For multilingual, use multilingual-e5-large or Cohere embed v3.
